clue.text: Injury for which Noel is treated

indicators.note: Noel and 'is' are treated, processed or worked on, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Noel is being treated in hospital for some harm he has suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like part of the sentence but joins Noel as fodder; 'treated' rearranges NOEL plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or damaged patch of tissue, a kind of physical harm.

clue.text: He sounds deep in the arms of Morpheus

definitions.text: He sounds deep in the arms of Morpheus

parts.words: He sounds deep in the arms of Morpheus
parts.note: Morpheus is the god of sleep, so this is someone making noises while sound asleep; 'deep' seems to describe his voice but means deeply asleep

explanation.surface: A man with a deep voice in the embrace of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes rasping breathing noises in deep slumber fits this description.

clue.text: Males without exception

parts.note: a phrase for all men, with no man left out, since every man had a mother

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single man, each and all of the male sex.

clue.text: Teaches about lost property, perhaps

indicators.note: about here means around, in a different order, so the letters of the word are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone instructs others about where to find mislaid belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but signals rearranging TEACHES.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, property reverting to the Crown or state when the owner dies without heirs is forfeited by the family, a kind of loss.

clue.text: Celebrating occasions chuck ers-out might enjoy

definitions.text: Celebrating occasions chuck ers-out might enjoy

parts.words: Celebrating occasions chuck ers-out might enjoy
parts.note: hosting festivities, read also as bouncers (chuckers-out) enjoying the ejection of people from a venue

explanation.surface: Bouncers would enjoy these celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'chuckers-out' split as 'chuck ers-out'; chuckers-out are bouncers, who like hurling people out.
explanation.definitionFit: To host festive gatherings is to give celebrations; bouncers literally hurl revellers.

clue.text: How to get a share of the play

definitions.text: How to get a share of the play

parts.words: How to get a share of the play
parts.note: to join in is to have a share of the action, and an actor gets a role in a play

explanation.surface: Asking how to obtain a portion of the drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means participate, and literally to accept a role in a stage production.

clue.text: Strikes a man of Tarsus in a saint's garb

indicators.note: the man of Tarsus is put inside the letters for 'a saint's', dressed in his garb

parts.note: A plus ST'S, the saint abbreviation with its possessive
Saul of Tarsus was the apostle Paul's original name

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a man from Tarsus who is dressed as a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garb' backs up 'in': SAUL wears the letters A, ST, S around him, sitting after the first AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are attacks or blows, as are strikes.

clue.text: Despite missing end of race. Vine's been in peak form

indicators.note: put into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word race is the one missing from the mix

explanation.surface: A man called Vine has been in excellent shape despite failing to finish a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak form' looks like one phrase but splits: 'peak' is the definition and 'form' rearranges VINESBEEN once the E ending 'race' is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Britain, in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Not in good voice staggering ashore

indicators.note: walking unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor coming ashore unsteadily, with a croaky voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, croaky voice is not a good speaking or singing voice.

clue.text: Common cry when fabulous bird turns round

indicators.note: the bird's name is turned to face the other way, read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A shout goes up when a legendary bird wheels about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' means vulgar or informal: COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor is an informal British exclamation, a working-class shout of astonishment.

clue.text: Replaced her chair for, divine ruler

indicators.note: placed again in another arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone swapped her seat for a holy leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or high church official who presides over others.

clue.text: Specified period some time in the future

definitions.meaning: a single span of twenty-four hours, named as such

explanation.surface: Contrasting a precise length of time with a vague future moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A twenty-four hour span is precisely stated; the phrase also means eventually, at an unnamed later time.

clue.text: Our unlearned friend and how he may express himself

definitions.text: Our unlearned friend and how he may express himself

parts.words: Our unlearned friend and how he may express himself
parts.note: an uneducated speaker who talks without regard to grammar

explanation.surface: Describing an uneducated acquaintance and the way he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with poor grammar is how someone without schooling might phrase things.

clue.text: Suffering from an allergy, possibly

indicators.note: the letters come from within the words that follow, across the break between them

explanation.surface: A person with hay fever or similar who might be in discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'allerGY Possibly'. GYP is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is informal British for pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Mechanical devices past President found in a bad state

indicators.note: the abbreviation is discovered sitting inside the jumbled letters
a state in poor condition, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for past president, used by clubs and societies

explanation.surface: Machinery and a former leader turn up in a nation in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges STATE to TAETS, and 'found in' places PP after TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappets are engine parts, levers or projections that move valves in a motor.

clue.text: One of royal blood with a thing about the Spanish

indicators.note: the letters of 'a thing' go round the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A royal person with a fixation on Spain's people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a thing about' suggests an obsession, but 'about' puts A THING around EL.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheling was an Anglo-Saxon prince or noble of the royal family.

clue.text: Fleet Street's ultimate deliverer?

parts.note: Fleet Street was the home of London's press; the last link in getting the press to readers is a youngster on a delivery round

explanation.surface: Asking who finally saves the newspaper industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliverer' suggests a saviour, but here it is the lad bringing the papers to the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad who brings newspapers to homes is the last step in a paper's distribution.

clue.text: Conceit revealing vitality in troubled times

indicators.note: the word for vitality is placed inside the jumbled letters
disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Vanity shows energy in difficult days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges TIMES to ETISM, and 'in' puts GO after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centredness and vanity, an inflated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Wrath that is about right

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes round the letter for right

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Anger that is roughly justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or fury, an old poetic word.

clue.text: Irrational as an individual having one over the eight

parts.note: I is one, a single individual
one more than eight is nine; the phrase also means drunk

explanation.surface: Someone being foolish as one person who has had a drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, but here it is simply NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid or silly, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Small fry providing pictorial evidence useful to the RSPCA?

definitions.text: providing pictorial evidence useful to the RSPCA?
definitions.meaning: photographers who catch people beating animals with whips; the RSPCA is Britain's animal welfare charity

explanation.surface: Young people who supply photos for an animal charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent young people are small fry; read as two words, photographers of those who lash animals.

clue.text: Stout, but largely the wine

definitions.meaning: a playful reading of the word as port plus -ly, as though mostly made of port

explanation.surface: A fat man who is mostly made of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints no letter count. The second sense reads the word as 'port-ish', a joke on a portly man filled with fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout and round-bodied; a heavy drinker of port might grow so.

clue.text: Stand up to relax one's inside!

indicators.note: the letters for one's go into the word for relax

parts.note: to rest is to relax
I'S, I as one, with the possessive

explanation.surface: An encouragement to unwind inner tension.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand, to refuse to give in.

clue.text: Shines dazzlingly with one of Elgar's variations

indicators.note: Elgar's Enigma Variations, here a cue that the letters vary in order

explanation.surface: A performance of one of the Enigma Variations is brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's 'Enigma Variations' is a famous orchestral work, but 'variations' rearranges ELGARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Glares are intense, blinding lights, so glaring is shining harshly.

clue.text: Sun-worshipper out of gear?

definitions.meaning: one who sunbathes, here without clothing
gear means clothes, so out of them is naked

explanation.surface: A sunbather whose car is in neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist sunbathes with no clothes, out of their gear.

clue.text: Single slipper

parts.note: one of a pair of runners that slide over snow

explanation.surface: One indoor shoe on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' is not footwear but a thing that slips, on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis come in pairs and glide over snow, so one is a lone thing that slides.

clue.text: I upset the Lone Ranger's friend completely

indicators.note: turned over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Tonto was the Lone Ranger's companion in the American Western series

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to upsetting a cowboy's sidekick totally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TONTO to NTOTO, placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for in total, entirely.

clue.text: Not required by sewers up to point

parts.note: needles are things that sew
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Something unnecessary for people who stitch, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains but means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary.
